2  THIS MFA IS FILED U/S.173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT,
AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 10.07.2018 PASSED IN MVC NO.1121/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL-II, BALLARI, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM  -3-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:12982-DB  MFA No. 100230 of 2019 PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KRISHNA S.DIXIT  AND  THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL)

This appeal by the claimants is filed against the judgment and award, dated 10.07.2018, passed in M.V.C. No.1121/2016 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-II, Ballari (for short, 'Tribunal') not being satisfied with the compensation awarded and seeking for higher compensation, and also challenging the finding of the Tribunal attributing contributory negligence on the deceased to the extent of 30%.
2.
Sri. Manjunath G.Patil, learned counsel appearing for the appellants, at the outset, submits that he does not press the ground of appeal insofar as challenging of liability is concerned.

Placing the said submission on record, we affirm the finding of the Tribunal with regard to contributory NC:
2024:KHC-D:12982-DB negligence, which is apportioned at 70% on the part of respondent No.1 (before the Tribunal) and 30% on the part of the deceased.
Now, the only question that is required to be considered in this appeal is with regard to the quantum of compensation.

3. Sri. Manjunath G.Patil, learned counsel for the appellants submits that the deceased was working as a driver of a lorry and was earning Rs.13,000/- per month; however, the Tribunal committed a grave error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month and , therefore, he prays that the income of the deceased be reassessed at a higher rate.

He further submits that the deceased was aged 25 years as per the Driving licence, but the Tribunal considering the Post-mortem Report has taken the age of the deceased as 26 years which has resulted in adopting wrong multiplier '17', and as such, he prays for adopting multiplier '18' having regard to the age of the deceased as 25 years.
On these grounds he seeks for enhancement of compensation by allowing the appeal.

sentences.text: Per Contra, Sri. R.R.Mane, learned counsel for Respondent No.3-insurance company supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal.

He submits that in the absence of any cogent evidence to prove the income of the deceased, the Tribunal has rightly assessed income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month, and the same needs no interference.
He further submits that the compensation awarded on other conventional heads is just and proper.
So contending, learned counsel seeks to dismiss the appeal.

5. We have heard Sri. Manjunath G.Patil, learned counsel for the appellants/claimants, and Sri.
R.R.Mane, learned counsel for the respondent No.3-insurance company.
Perused the appeal papers and the material made available by the learned counsel for the appellants.
6. A claim petition being filed by the parents and sister of the deceased Mohammed Ghouse seeking compensation for the death of said Mohammed Ghouse.
The claimants had arrayed the wife of the deceased as respondent No.6 to the claim petition.
On issuance of notice, the claim petition was contested and evidence was recorded.
The NC: 2024:KHC-D:12982-DB Tribunal considering the evidence on record, assessed compensation at Rs.19,97,800/-.

Insofar as liability is concerned, the Tribunal has held that drivers of both the lorries were negligent to the extent of 70% on the part of respondent No.1 (before the Tribunal) and 30% on the part of the deceased who was driving lorry.
Hence, the Tribunal held that the claimants were entitled for 70% of compensation assessed by it with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
7. The claimants claimed that the deceased was working as a driver of lorry and was earning a sum of Rs.13,000/- per month.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month.
However, considering that the deceased was a driver, in the facts and circumstances of the case, we reassess the income of the deceased at Rs.12,000/- per month.

Considering the Driving Licence of the deceased made available by the learned counsel for the appellants during the course of hearing, which indicates that the deceased was aged 25 years, the appropriate multiplier applicable would be '18'. The Tribunal has rightly added 40% of the assessed income towards 'loss NC: 2024:KHC-D:12982-DB of future prospects of the deceased'.
There is no dispute with regard to deduction of 1/4th of the assessed income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.

8. Having assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.12,000/- per month, the claimants would be entitled for modified compensation of Rs.27,21,600/- [Rs.12,000/- + 40% x 12 x 18 x 3/4] on the head 'loss of dependency'
9.

There are four dependants i.e., appellants/claimants No.1 to 3 and respondent No.6, but the Tribunal has erred in awarding compensation under the head 'loss of consortium' only to respondent No.6 i.e., the wife of the deceased.

In view of the judgment of the Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram & Others1, the appellants/claimants and respondent No.6 are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- each (Rs.40,000 + 10%) towards 'loss of parental, filial & spousal consortium.

sentences.text: Further, the appellants are entitled to a sum of Rs.16,500 (Rs.15,000 + 10% escalation) each towards 'loss of estate' and 'funeral expenses.

sentences.text:
Thus, the appellants/claimants and respondent No.6 would be entitled to modified compensation as under:
 Particulars Amount  (in Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 27,21,600/-
 Loss of estate 16,500/-
 Funeral expenses 16,500/-
Loss of parental, filial & spousal consortium 1,76,000/-
 (Rs.44,000/- x 4)

Total 29,30,600/-
Since we have affirmed the finding of the Tribunal with regard to contributory negligence, the appellants/claimants and respondent No.6 shall be entitled to total compensation of Rs.20,51,420/-
(being 70% of Rs.29,30,600/-) as against Rs.13,98,460/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

11. In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal  is modified to the extent that the  appellants/claimants and respondent No.6 are  NC: 2024:KHC-D:12982-DB entitled to total compensation of Rs.20,51,420/- as against Rs.13,98,460/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.

Draw modified award accordingly.
